# SimEx: instructions for GitHub Copilot

SimEx is a personal research tool for testing the owner's own AI traders against a live market:
live Gemini market data, simulated money, honest fills. It is not a product and has no users
other than the owner.

Read [`docs/PLAN.md`](../docs/PLAN.md) for scope and the build plan, and [`docs/adr/`](../docs/adr/)
for decisions already made. **Do not re-open an accepted ADR without saying so explicitly.**
This file duplicates the hard rules from [`CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md); keep the two in step.

## Hard rules

- **Money is `Decimal`, never float**, in the ledger, matching engine, fees and balances
  (ADR 0004). Serialize decimals as strings.
- **Simulation only.** Never add code that places real orders or moves real money (ADR 0002).
- **Only the ingestor talks to an exchange.** Every other component reads from Kafka and must not
  depend on which venue the data came from.
- **Personal use only (ADR 0010).** No public leaderboard, public sign-up, downloadable
  recordings, or public page showing market data or results derived from it. Any web UI is
  private.
- **Never commit market data**: no recordings, feed dumps or fixtures copied from a live feed.
  Test fixtures are hand-written or synthetic. `data/` and `*.parquet` are gitignored.
- **Coinbase data never feeds agents, the matching engine or scoring.** Coinbase's terms forbid
  using its data to benchmark AI agents. The Coinbase adapter is off by default, is for feed
  research only, and publishes to `research.coinbase.md.*`.
- **One writer per trading pair for books and matching.** Balances are owned by a per-account
  writer (ADR 0014): cash is shared across pairs, so it is the one deliberate exception. Pair
  engines never touch balances; they report fills to the account writer. Don't fold the account
  writer into the pair engines.
- **Never commit secrets**: no `.env`, keys (`*.key`, `*.pem`), tokens or passwords. Use
  `.env.example` for placeholders.
- **No AI attribution** anywhere: no `Co-Authored-By` trailers, no "Generated with" or
  "Generated by" footers in commit messages, PR descriptions, issues or issue comments. If a tool
  appends one, remove it before the work is considered done.
- **Commits are authored by the owner**, `Abhitej S <suddhaabhitej@gmail.com>`, never by an AI
  tool. Check `git config user.email` before the first commit of a session.

## Workflow

- Never commit to `main`. Branch as `<type>/<short-name>` (`feat/`, `fix/`, `docs/`, `infra/`).
- One issue, one PR. Reference it (`Closes #N`).
- Before opening a PR: `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` and `pytest` must all pass.
- A significant design choice gets a short ADR in `docs/adr/` from `template.md`, plus a row in
  `docs/adr/README.md`. If it changes an accepted ADR, mark that ADR amended or superseded in
  both the ADR and the index.
- **Propose before building.** For anything non-trivial, write the design in the issue or PR
  first and wait for the owner's approval. The owner reviews designs, not just diffs.
- **If a task is ambiguous, ask.** Do not guess at a constant, a threshold or a venue behaviour.

## How this project decides things

These habits are why the codebase is correct, not incidental style. Keep them.

- **Measure, don't assume.** Every constant below came from live data or a tool in `tools/`. When
  a new constant is needed, write a tool that measures it, run it on recordings, and record the
  distribution in an ADR. Do not pick a round number.
- **Say what you could not verify.** If a claim rests on docs, memory or a guess, label it as
  such. Several real bugs here were found because a guess was flagged and then tested.
- **Prove the tests can fail.** After writing a safeguard, break it on purpose and confirm a test
  catches it. Property tests that pass while exercising nothing are worse than none.
- **Honest over flattering.** Where a simulation detail is unknowable from public data, pick the
  pessimistic reading, make the alternative a config switch, and report both.

## Stack and environment

- Python 3.12+, asyncio. Package code in `src/simex/<component>/`, tests in `tests/`, one-off
  measurement tools in `tools/`.
- Infrastructure is Docker Compose (`compose.yaml`): Kafka (KRaft), Postgres, Valkey, Prometheus,
  Grafana. Ports bind to `127.0.0.1`.
- Production target: Oracle Cloud Always Free, **ARM64, 2 cores, 12 GB RAM**. Every image must
  support `linux/arm64` and every service needs a memory limit. Development is on an x86 Windows
  laptop, so keep everything multi-arch and test Windows paths (CI has a `test-windows` job).
- Market data: Gemini public WebSocket `wss://ws.gemini.com`, no auth. Pairs BTCUSD, ETHUSD,
  SOLUSD, normalized everywhere else as `BTC-USD` etc.
- Prometheus alert rules live in `infra/prometheus/rules/` with `promtool` tests in
  `infra/prometheus/tests/`. Every new alert needs a test.

## Measured constants — do not change without re-measuring

All measured on live Gemini between 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-19. Each is recorded with its
distribution in the ADR named.

**Feed (ADR 0011)**
- level2 about 9 msg/s per pair (28 msg/s total); trades only **4 to 11 per minute per pair**.
  Anything that waits for trades must tolerate minutes of silence. The stale-data check must use
  level2 and ping only, **never** `market_trades`.
- Raw about 2 GB/day; recorded about 0.55 GB/day as zstd Parquet.
- Lag, clock-corrected: depth p50 51 ms / p99 155 ms; trades p50 40 ms / p99 105 ms.
- Gemini update IDs are a **single exchange-wide counter**, not per product. Each diff starts
  exactly where the previous one for that symbol ended (`U == previous u`, 100% over 8,477
  diffs). A snapshot is a `depthUpdate` with `U == u` carrying the full book. A gap is
  `U > previous u`, and the missing count is **unknowable** (record it as null).
- Gap resync by per-product resubscribe: 72–435 ms, mean 161 ms. Scheduled snapshot refresh:
  78–156 ms.

**Book and audit (ADR 0009, 0012)**
- About 285 B per level; about 2.4 MB for all three books; about 65 µs to apply one event.
- Audits align about 64% of the time; the rest are `inside_diff`, because Gemini answers a depth
  request at request time while the stream batches every 100 ms. Gate: 0 mismatches and at least
  10 aligned audits per product per hour.
- The three pairs hash onto **two** of the three `md.level2` partitions.

**Fill model (ADR 0014)**
- Instrument grids, confirmed live 2026-10-18 against `api.gemini.com/v1/symbols/details`.
  Note Gemini's naming is inverted from the usual: `tick_size` is the **size** increment and
  `quote_increment` is the **price** tick.

  | Pair | Price tick | Size increment | Min size |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | BTC-USD | 0.01 | 0.00000001 | 0.00001 |
  | ETH-USD | 0.01 | 0.000001 | 0.001 |
  | SOL-USD | 0.001 | 0.000001 | 0.001 |

- Fees: **60 bps maker, 120 bps taker** (entry tier, schedule dated 2026-09-01). A round trip
  costs 1.8–2.4%, so fees dominate most strategies. Scoring must always report gross P&L, fee
  drag and net P&L separately.
- Fill/cancel match window `W = 300 ms`, from a 28-hour measurement (|print − shrink| p90 is
  146–203 ms).
- About **99.9% of level shrinks are cancels, not fills.** Almost all book activity is requoting.
- 17.3% / 12.8% / 5.1% of print quantity (BTC/ETH/SOL) matches no shrink: hidden or instantly
  replenished liquidity, and a hard ceiling on what any book-based simulator can explain here.
- A book cross alone **does not fill** (`EXCHANGE_BOOK_CROSS=print` default). It sets the order to
  the front of the queue; only prints at or through its price fill it. Filling on a cross was
  tried and produced 97–100% invented maker fills.
- Resulting maker behaviour: 95–98% of maker fills come from trade-throughs; fill rates 73/57/52%
  at 300 s; markouts 1–5 bp **worse** than real makers, which is the intended pessimistic side.
- The honesty check validates fill **quality** (markout vs real prints), not fill **frequency**.
  Frequency is unverifiable without a real account and is the largest open assumption.

**Live runner (ADR 0015)**
- Hold-back **250 ms**, set from the delivery tail (99.973% under 100 ms, about 99.99% under
  250 ms). Watermark lag about 0.25–0.27 s; an order takes effect about 0.45 s after submission.
- Late records mean the ordering **margin** was lost, not the order. The guarantee for orders is
  statistical, not absolute. Alert on a rate (>20 in 10 min), not on any occurrence.
- Anti-cheat delay **200 ms**, applied to orders **and cancels**. Re-measure on Oracle.

## Windows notes

- `scripts/dev.ps1` sets `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"`, so it cannot be used with `2>&1 |`
  redirection. Run the modules directly when teeing output.
- No directory `fsync` on Windows; use `os.replace` for atomic renames.
- Use `time.perf_counter`, not `time.monotonic`: the latter only ticks about every 15.6 ms.
- Windows refuses to delete open files, so any cleanup path must catch `OSError` and continue.

## Commands

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,analysis]"
ruff check . && ruff format --check . && pytest
docker compose up -d
python -m simex.ingest      # also: simex.book, simex.recorder, simex.exchange
```
